newsitem.title: UK: Aegis posts higher profits, buys U.S. firm.
newsitem.headline: Aegis posts higher profits, buys U.S. firm.

text.p: Aegis Group, parent company of the Carat media planning and buying network, on Tuesday reported a 15 percent rise in first-half profits and said it is entering the U.S. market with the purchase of a New York-based media buying firm.
Pre-tax profits for the 1996 first-half rose to 18.7 million pounds ($29 million) from 16.3 million, and turnover gained eight percent to 1.81 billion pounds from 1.67 billion.
The group marked its continued improvement by restoring dividends and making an interim payment of 0.25 pence. Aegis' shares fell one pence to 64.5 pence.
The company said it is making its first foray into the U.S. market with the acquisition of New York-based Media Buying Services, a privately-owned company with annual billings of about $160 million.
Aegis chief executive Crispin Davis said the company paid about $5 million for the firm.
"It's relatively small," Davis told Reuters. "But it has good clients -- Westinghouse, Saks Fifth Avenue, MCI. Over time I think we can develop this business into a substantial one."

Aegis began looking at possible U.S. acquisitions about 12 months ago. The media specialist market in the U.S. remains undeveloped, with advertising agencies handling most media buying. "Media specialists have about 65 percent of the European market," said Davis. "In the U.S. it's about 10 percent."
But the increasing complexity and fragmentation of the media market is raising the need for specialists to help companies get better results from their advertising.

A growing number of television channels, proliferation of magazines, increasing numbers of radio stations, as well as the advent of the Internet and home shopping is increasing the need for specialist services.

Davis said Aegis plans to use Media Buying Services as its initial foothold in the U.S. market and aims to grow the business organically. "But I would rule out other acquisitions if something suitable came up," he said.

Davis said he was happy with Aegis' first-half results, although he now expects the European display advertising market to increase by only four percent in 1996. Aegis earlier had forecast six percent growth in the European market.
"I think the four percent rather than the six percent reflects slightly sluggish economic growth, particularly in Germany," Davis said. "The rest of Europe is pretty much as we anticipated."
Britain and France were particularly strong markets for Aegis in the 1996 first half, with each posting double digit growth.
"As far as we're concerned we were able to deliver a pretty good set of results despite an average market," Davis said.
He said he expects European display advertising to rise five to six percent in 1997.
"I would expect over the next 18 months we would see a slight strengthening," Davis said.

Aegis is experiencing strong growth in Eastern Europe. "The market is growing very fast, between 20 and 30 percnet, and we are gaining share in these markets very rapidly," Davis said. Aegis' own operations in Eastern Europe are growing at 30 to 50 percent.

Eastern Europe remains a small part of Aegis' total business, accounting for less than five percent of the total. "But over the next few years we see it becoming quite significant," Davis said. "I think five years from now Eastern Europe will be more than 10 percent of our European business." ($1=.6412 Pound)
